sources.title: Water Quality and Hydroclimatic Dataset for Rivers and Streams of Dhaka, Bangladesh
sources.authors: Parishmita Sinha; Nirab Debnath; Prithwiraj Bhattacharjee
sources.size: 1,495 records; 58 coordinate pairs; 60 river/location name combinations; 104 dates
sources.used: GIS; pH/DO/COD screening; DO model training and temporal evaluation
sources.transform: Normalize Tongi Khal casing; flag six invalid negative-value rows; retain raw file; do not use supplied WQI or Pollution_Label; keep unspecified nutrient chemical forms out of objective comparisons.
sources.limits: Repository-published measurements, not independently verified lab results. Original QA/custody documentation is incomplete. Historical, geographically limited and temporally clustered.

sources.title: Dataset for the BASIS Framework: High-Resolution Spatial, Diurnal, and Hydraulic Fecal Pollution Tracking in Resource-Limited Urban Channels
sources.authors: Bijit Kumar Banik; Rahul Das Gupta; Md. Hasibul Chowdhury; Imran Hasan; Md. Imran Kabir; Muhammad Azizul Hoque
sources.size: Seven worksheets; extracted 40 velocity points, six hydraulic groups and 62 unlocated quality samples
sources.period: February 2025 quality campaign; May 16, 2025 velocity survey; hydraulic-group timestamps absent
sources.used: Separate survey GIS layer; mixing/closure investigation examples; explicit unlocated-sample audit
sources.transform: Read published mean concentrations; multiply FC means by 10^5 to CFU/100 mL; do not count replicates as independent sites; do not join survey numeric IDs to quality-station IDs.
sources.limits: No industrial-emitter labels. The actual quality worksheet lacks the coordinates suggested in broad metadata. No invented geolocation or complete urban-drain topology.

sources.title: NASA POWER monthly PRECTOTCORR at 22.57 N, 89.51 E
sources.license: NASA data attribution; source terms apply
sources.transform: Convert mm/day monthly means to mm/month using calendar day counts; thresholds computed only from training.
sources.limits: Gridded model-derived data, not a local rain gauge; historical revisions and current endpoints can change. Not a live tank-stock feed.

sources.title: NOAA CPC Relative Oceanic Nino Index historical table
sources.period: Historical table used for lagged 1984–2025 experiment
sources.used: Candidate climate feature and baseline comparison
sources.transform: Index values by center month; target-month minus three lag, with season ending before target.
sources.limits: Modern historical revisions; not as-issued hindcasts. RONI addition did not improve Brier loss. No local storm/salinity attribution.

sources.title: Bangladesh Environment Conservation Rules 2023
sources.authors: Government of Bangladesh / Bangladesh Government Press
sources.license: Official regulatory reference; no endorsement implied
sources.size: 107-page Gazette PDF; relevant table on PDF p.53 / printed p.3061
sources.used: pH 6–9, DO >=5 mg/L and COD <=50 mg/L screening objectives
sources.transform: Visual transcription from the rendered table; no reliance on garbled extracted Bengali text.
sources.limits: Only three matched parameters used. Intended use is inland fisheries. This is not finished drinking-water assessment, effluent compliance or a legal finding about pre-2023 samples.

sources.title: Climate++ fictional water-continuity network on Dacope roads (GeoPackage)
sources.license: Synthetic layers: project terms to be set by the team. Embedded road geometry is OpenStreetMap, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (HOT export). Dacope boundary from the HDX Bangladesh administrative boundaries; confirm its licence on the HDX dataset page.
sources.size: 13 layers; 6 network nodes, 2 catchments, 3 hazard polygons, 18 access rows
sources.used: Antar Dacope calamity service-point template, retained historical library, and real road graph used by V3 response map and private operations
sources.transform: Nodes and polygons digitised in QGIS on OSM roads (snapped); shortest paths on the road network, with storm polygons removed from the roads by geometric difference; scripts/build-gis-network.py converts the layers to JSON and applies the stated speed and thresholds. v0.4 independently exports 927 source roads into 1,425 nodes/1,563 edges; 1,514 support vehicle road profile. Shared-coordinate grade rules, bridge endpoint ramp assumptions, bidirectional inference for missing one-way values, speed caps and snap limits are documented in docs/ROAD-GRAPH.md. V3 preserves Antar handoff-v2 service coordinates/hazard vertices; source references/hashes are retained at research/gis/antar-v2. Other towns use independent OSM roads, not translated Dacope geometry.
sources.limits: Fictional network and hazard polygons; not a forecast and not an operating system. Speed is one assumed value for all roads; thresholds are scenario assumptions. OSM completeness is unverified; nothing is validated on the ground. No current traffic, flood-safe route, vehicle access, supplier operation, reserve stock or drinking-water clearance is established. Route alternatives use shared-edge penalties, not independently verified disaster corridors.

sources.title: Bangladesh-River-Pollution-GIS coordinate classifications
sources.license: MIT declared by publisher metadata; constituent data terms not independently established
sources.period: Publisher updated 2025-09-07; no sampling dates supplied
sources.used: Separate research-context GIS layer and investigation-distance queries
sources.transform: Preserve all valid coordinates and published values/classes; retain the #N/A class as Unclassified. No imputed pollutants, sampling dates or health-risk labels. Large true-colour imagery not downloaded.
sources.limits: No stated pollutant units, laboratory validation or classification method; Low/Very Low do not establish clean water. No live pollution or human-health exposure inference.

sources.title: WPdx+ Bangladesh historical water-point inventory
sources.authors: WPdx / Global Water Challenge; original providers UNHCR, REACH Initiative and WaterAid
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 per WPdx Provider Agreement: https://www.waterpointdata.org/share-data/
sources.size: 20,084 unique point IDs and coordinate pairs
sources.used: Historical candidate locator with radius-limited straight-line distances, source dates and confirmation-required labels
sources.transform: Allowlist of coordinates, IDs, dates, organisational providers, source/technology and administrative labels. No personal contacts, notes or photos. Source-presence and cleaned-condition fields are not equated.
sources.limits: No current quality clearance or availability. 90.8% of points are in Cox’s Bazar; no Dacope-labelled records. Absence means inventory coverage is missing, not that water supplies do not exist.

operationalEvidence.safeWaterClearance: No current validated clearance feed; never inferred from these datasets

regionalExpansion.meaning: Five bounded real road regions; six fictional service roles in each. Original pollution coordinates are never relocated.
regionalExpansion.assetTruth: Scenario assets/hazards, not surveyed facilities or live warnings
regionalExpansion.pollutionInput: Validated CSV/GeoJSON point fields and authenticated private observations; entered values not independently authenticated
